property_summary: The transferOwnership function should only revert when newOwner is the zero address when called by the owner.
addReward always succeeds (does not revert) for any previously unregistered reward token.
owner() should always be non-zero after a successful addReward call
A non-owner call to transferOwnership reverb for any newOwner that is not the zero address.
addReward does not change the owner address
After calling addReward, the rewardDistributor remains the same as set in setUp.
After calling addReward for any reward token, the rewardDistributor address remains unchanged from its original value.
After calling addReward on a valid reward token, the rewardDistributor remains equal to the contract's own address (i.e., address(this)).
After any successful addReward call, the rewardDistributor remains unchanged from its previous value.
After addReward is called, the rewardDistributor address must equal the contract's own address (address(this)).
The contract's rewardDistributor should never be the zero address after any sequence of operations ending with addReward.
After a call to addReward, claimableRewards for any account on any reward token is unchanged.
After a call to addReward, the caller's own claimableRewards balance for any reward token remains unchanged.
After addReward, the caller's balance of each reward token (IERC20) remains unchanged.
After addReward, the staking token balance of the caller does not decrease.
After addReward, the sum of claimableRewards for any fixed address and reward token over all stakers is unchanged.
After calling addReward, the migrator address is always the zero address regardless of setMigrator calls.
The balanceOf function returns the balance of the given account parameter, not the caller.
The balanceOf function returns the same value for any two different accounts that have the same actual balance.
The balanceOf function returns the correct balance for any account, including the zero address.
The balanceOf function returns the same value for two different accounts that staked the same amount.
balanceOf returns the same value for any account before and after staking an amount that does not belong to that account.
Adding the same reward token address again does not increase the length of the rewardTokens array.
Adding a reward token that already exists does not change the rewardTokens array length.
After calling addReward(token), the rewardData[token].lastUpdateTime equals the current block timestamp.
Calling addReward(token) twice with the same token increases rewardTokens.length by exactly 1 on the second call (instead of 0), which the reference prevents by reverting.
addReward always reverts when called by the owner.
After a revert from addReward, the reward token list must remain unchanged.
After calling addReward twice with the same token address, rewardTokens length must increase by 2 (the second call must not be silently skipped).
Calling addReward with a new token always increases rewardTokens.length by 1.
Every call to addReward(a) with a token address a that is not already in the reward tokens list results in an extension of the rewardTokens array.
After calling addReward(token) with any token address, the last element of rewardTokens equals that token address.
After calling addReward with the same token address twice, the token appears at least once in the rewardTokens array.
For any reward token after it has been added, rewardPerToken returns a value greater than or equal to the stored rewardPerTokenStored.
Before any reward is notified, rewardPerToken for any reward token equals its stored rewardPerTokenStored value.
After adding a new reward token, calling rewardPerToken on that token returns a value that is equal to the stored rewardPerTokenStored for that token (i.e., 0 initially).

For any reward token, the public rewardPerToken function returns the same value as the stored rewardPerTokenStored for that token when no time has passed since the last update (i.e., block.timestamp == lastUpdateTime).
After adding a reward token, the public rewardPerToken function should return the same value as the stored rewardPerTokenStored when the total supply is zero.
After addReward is called for a token, rewardPeriodFinish returns at least the current block timestamp (since it is set to block.timestamp + DURATION).

After addReward is called for a token, rewardPeriodFinish returns a value strictly greater than the stored lastUpdateTime for that token (since periodFinish is set to block.timestamp + DURATION, while lastUpdateTime is set to block.timestamp).
After addReward is called for a token, rewardPeriodFinish returns block.timestamp + DURATION.

After calling addReward for a token, calling rewardPeriodFinish on that token returns a value that is at least block.timestamp (since periodFinish is set to block.timestamp + DURATION, which is >= block.timestamp).

After addReward(token) is called, rewardPeriodFinish(token) returns a value equal to rewardData[token].periodFinish, which is block.timestamp + DURATION (86400 * 7) at the time of the call, and is strictly greater than the stored rewardData[token].lastUpdateTime (which equals block.timestamp).
The contract's own balance of stakingToken should never decrease after a staker calls stakeFor.
The caller's staking token balance should decrease by exactly the staked amount after stakeFor is called by the caller.
After any stakeFor call, the total supply of staked tokens equals the contract's staking token balance.
After staking, the staking token balance of the caller must decrease by the staked amount.
After any stakeFor call, the contract's staking token balance increases by exactly the staked amount.
After addReward, calling notifyRewardAmount with the same reward token address must succeed (not revert).
After addReward(token), the rewardData[token].lastUpdateTime must be equal to block.timestamp.
After addReward(token) returns, the rewardData[token].lastUpdateTime stored in the contract must be block.timestamp.
After addReward(token) is called, calling notifyRewardAmount for a different token that was never added must revert.
After addReward(token) is called, the rewardData[token].lastUpdateTime is set to block.timestamp.
After a call to addReward, the earned value for a staker is consistent with the reward per token and the user's balance.
After addReward, the sum of claimableRewards for the zero address across all reward tokens is zero.
After addReward, the user's claimableRewards for the new reward token is zero for the zero address.
After adding a reward token via addReward, the rewardPerToken for that token is equal to rewardPerTokenStored stored in the contract.
After addReward, the reward per token stored for the new token equals the reward per token calculated for that token.
After addReward, the staking token balance of the zero address remains zero (no tokens are sent to address(0)).
After addReward, the migrator address remains address(0) (zero address) if never set.
After addReward, the totalSupply change equals the balanceOf change for the staker address.
The total supply after addReward is equal to the sum of balances of all users (the only addresses that can have a positive balance are those of the caller and possibly the zero address).
After adding a reward token, the reward data for that token has a non-zero lastUpdateTime.
After calling addReward, the state variable migrator is never set by that function, so it remains the zero address.
After addReward, the migrator address is unchanged (remains address(this) from setUp).
After addReward, calling migrateStake with the contract's own address as oldStaking should not reduce the total supply.
After addReward, migrating with the contract's own staking address must not change the caller's staking balance.
After addReward, the rewardPerTokenStored for the reward token should be zero.
